_**Agent (claude-4.6-opus-high-thinking)**_

Here is what was going wrong and what we changed.

## Cause

1. **`ev_process_due` order**  
   It always runs the **smallest `fire_at` first**. `PRESS` before `STRUM` only applies when **`fire_at` is equal**. If an older **`EVT_STRUM`** was at 200 ms and the next chord’s **`EVT_PRESS`** was at 201 ms, the **strum ran first**, so it looked like “strum before frets.”

2. **Strike tied to first touch**  
   Using `chord_start_ms + STRUM_DELAY_MS` fixed the strike relative to the **first** sample in the chord window, while the chord is only finalized **`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` later**. That didn’t break ordering by itself, but it didn’t match “strike when the chord is locked” either.

## Changes

1. **Strike anchored to commit**  
   `strike_at` is now `now + STRUM_DELAY_MS` when the chord window closes, so “strike line” is **`STRUM_DELAY_MS` after the chord is committed**, not after the first edge. `FRET_EARLY_MS` is still “fret outputs this many ms before that strike.”

2. **Align with any pending strum**  
   Before enqueueing the new chord, we scan the queue for the latest **`EVT_STRUM`**. If the new **`press_at` would be strictly after** that strum’s `fire_at`, we set **`press_at` to that strum’s `fire_at`** so they share a tick; on a tie, **`PRESS` still runs before `STRUM`**.

3. **Header**  
   `STRUM_DELAY_MS` is documented as ms **from chord window close (commit)** to the strike/strum, not from the first note.

```164:202:/Users/greg/projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c
static void chord_commit(uint32_t now)
{
    /* Strike time first — never compute (strike_at - FRET_EARLY) in one uint32 step:
       if STRUM_DELAY < FRET_EARLY it underflows, press_at becomes huge and strum order
       breaks. Strike is anchored to chord commit (window just closed) so frets/strum
       are scheduled relative to when the chord is known, not first touch. */
    uint32_t strike_at = now + STRUM_DELAY_MS;
    ...
    if (have_pending_strum && (int32_t)(press_at - latest_pending_strum) > 0)
        press_at = latest_pending_strum;
    if ((int32_t)(press_at - now) < 0)
        press_at = now;

    uint32_t strum_at = strike_at;
    if ((int32_t)(strum_at - (press_at + FRET_EARLY_MS)) < 0)
        strum_at = press_at + FRET_EARLY_MS;
```

**Feel/timing:** Frets and strum are **`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` (40 ms) later** than before relative to the first finger, because the strike is measured from **commit**. If you want the same absolute latency from first touch as before, reduce `STRUM_DELAY_MS` by about `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` (e.g. 200 → 160) and tune from there.

_**Agent (claude-4.6-opus-high-thinking)**_

Here’s the actual reason it could happen:

## 1. The queue only ties on the **same** millisecond

`ev_process_due` always handles the **soonest** `fire_at` first. Only when **two events share the same** `fire_at` does it use priority: `PRESS` → `STRUM` → `RELEASE`.

So if **`EVT_STRUM` is at time 200** and **`EVT_PRESS` is at 201**, the dispatcher runs **strum first**, then press on the next tick. Same chord or not — **type order does not help** when the times differ.

## 2. Where those mismatched times came from

**Most common in your setup:** a **strum from an earlier chord** was still in the queue, while the **next chord’s frets** were scheduled **slightly later** (e.g. one chord’s strum at 200 ms, next chord’s press at 201 ms). The strum wasn’t “wrong math” for the new chord — it was **still the previous chord’s strum**, firing **before** the new chord’s presses because **200 &lt; 201**.

**Less common:** bad `press_at` / `strum_at` math (e.g. underflow when `STRUM_DELAY_MS &lt; FRET_EARLY_MS`) — your code even had a comment about that — could put strum **before** press in one chord. With your current constants that’s not the usual case.

So in short: **strum before note** happened because **strum’s scheduled time was earlier than the fret press’s time**, and the runner always does **earliest time first**; **PRESS-before-STRUM only applies when both fire in the same millisecond.**
